title: Streamline ranked_results payload and clarify cursor semantics for progressive fetch
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Refactor the reranking endpoint's output and pagination ergonomics to make progressive fetching predictable, lower client integration friction, and enable streaming while preserving stable ordering across pages and model rollouts.
background: Current rerank responses mix ad-hoc fields and rely on continuation tokens whose semantics are underspecified. Clients have reported surprising reordering between pages, inconsistent scores between streaming chunks and final responses, and difficulty supporting incremental fetches for large K. This causes higher implementation complexity in downstream apps, incorrect UI behavior (items jumping), and extra engineering effort for stability guarantees.
proposal_summary: 1) Define an explicit ranked_results payload schema with required fields (id, score, sort_key, provenance, metadata) and optional explain object. 2) Standardize top_k semantics: server honors requested top_k as a client hint but may clamp to configured max_k; response must include returned_count and requested_k. 3) Introduce a deterministic, forward-only cursor token that contains the last returned score and last_item_sort_key; clients can use it for pagination or progressive consumption. 4) Support streaming partial batches with a progressive_cursor that is safe for early stop and resume. 5) Document model+version incompatibility rules for cursor invalidation.
api_examples:
REQUEST example:
POST /v1/rerank HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "query": "what are good batteries for cold weather",
  "candidates": [{"id":"doc:123","embedding":[...]},{"id":"doc:456","embedding":[...]},...],
  "top_k": 50,
  "max_return": 10,  "# client requests first page only"
  "stream": true
}

RESPONSE page fetch using cursor (non-stream):
POST /v1/rerank?page_cursor=eyJsYXN0X3Njb3JlIjoxNjIsImxhc3RvbWtleSI6IjEyMyJ9 HTTP/1.1
{ "requested_k": 50, "max_return": 10 }
=> returns next 10, progressive_cursor updated or null when complete
acceptance_criteria: Schema: ranked_results is an array of objects with required string id, numeric score, numeric sort_key, string provenance.source, optional object explain. Responses include requested_k and returned_count fields.

Cursor: page_cursor is opaque to clients, base64-encoded JSON with at minimum {last_score, last_sort_key, model_version}. The server must validate model_version and reject cursors produced by incompatible model versions with 410 (Gone) and a clear migration message.

Stability: When using page_cursor, items across pages must be stable (no duplication, no skipping) given the same model_version and candidate set. Deterministic tie-breaking uses sort_key then candidate id.

Streaming: progressive_cursor can be used to resume from a streamed chunk and must be safe even if the stream is terminated early. Partial streaming must not produce final responses that reorder previously emitted items.
Top_k semantics documented: requested_k is honored as best-effort; responses include max_server_k and may include a reason field if clamped.

Performance: median end-to-end latency for non-streamed page requests (max_return<=10) remains <= 60ms on our standard profile; p99 <= 350ms. Rerank throughput must scale without 2x regressions vs baseline for common batch sizes.
Backward compatibility: Existing clients without cursor support continue to get full page responses. Deprecated fields removed only after two release cycles and with migration docs.
technical_notes: Cursor payload minimal shape: {"last_score": number, "last_sort_key": number, "model_version": "v1.18", "candidate_hash": "sha256"}. base64(json) opaque token. Keep payload small to reduce cookie/url length issues.

Sort key derivation: for sequences where a natural stable order does not exist, compute sort_key = (timestamp_ms << 16) | (stable_counter & 0xFFFF). This preserves insertion order deterministicly across reranks.
Server-side clamp: expose config param max_server_k per tenant; when requested_k > max_server_k, return header X-Rerank-Clamped: true and response.clamp_reason:"quota" or "capacity".

Streaming implementation: use ordered chunking from the sorted candidate list. Emit chunks with progressive_cursor tied to last emitted item. Use idempotent chunk offsets to support at-least-once delivery but make client dedupe easy via stable sort_key+id pair.

Model-version migration: when we update scoring model or embedding index, invalidate cursors by bumping model_version or candidate_hash. Servers must return HTTP 410 + body {"message":"cursor invalid due to model change", "migrate_to_fetch_all": true}.
Explainability: keep explain objects off by default (heavy). Add explain: "lite" option to return sparse weight breakdown; full explain behind eval-only flag for internal use.
Testing: add deterministic end-to-end tests that replay a known candidate set and assert no reordering across pages for top_k <= 200. Add fuzz tests for cursor corruption and model mismatch paths.
implementation_tasks: API: Define and publish updated OpenAPI schema for rerank endpoint (contract PR).
Server: Implement cursor encode/decode, model_version validation, and clamp headers.
Runtime: Update sorting pipeline to emit stable sort_key and deterministic tie-breaker. Add efficient compare ops for incremental extraction.
Streaming: Add progressive_cursor field in stream chunks and ensure chunk emission is ordered and checkpointed.
Docs: Write migration guide with examples, migration timeline, and sample client code snippets (JS/Python).
QA: Add load tests for streaming and paged flows with top_k=100/500 and ensure latency targets hold.
SDKs: Patch JS and Python SDKs to parse progressive_cursor and expose typed helpers for resume/consume semantics.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Launch schema changes behind a feature flag for 10% of requests. Monitor reordering, duplication, and latency metrics.
Phase 2 (opt-in): SDKs shipped with helpers. Announce migration docs and encourage clients to adopt progressive_cursor for large K.
Phase 3 (default): Make new schema default. Old response fields remain for two release cycles; deprecation warnings emitted in response headers.
Phase 4: Remove deprecated fields after client adoption thresholds are met.
testing_plan: Unit tests for cursor encode/decode across model_version values and corrupted token inputs.
Integration tests: end-to-end rerank with streaming + resume that validate no duplicates and monotonic score boundaries per page.
Performance tests: synthetic candidate sets of sizes [50, 500, 2000] measuring median/p99 for non-streamed and streamed flows.
Canary monitoring: dashboards for reorder_rate, cursor_error_rate, median_latency_top10, p99_latency_all. Set automated rollback if reorder_rate > 0.1% or cursor_error_rate spikes > 0.5%.
Client SDK tests: sample app that demonstrates pause/resume using progressive_cursor and de-duplication guidance.
docs_and_links: Related tickets: ENG-33147 (refactor ranking request model), ENG-36109 (rework rerank IO format), ENG-41207 (topk backpressure).
notes: Do not conflate progressive_cursor with continuation tokens used for re-ranking long-running background jobs — separate token namespaces to avoid accidental resume across different processes.
We should consider adding a compact bit-packed cursor format in a follow-up if token size becomes a problem for very deep pagination.
Customer ask: a large search customer wants deterministic UI for infinite scroll; prioritize POC with that tenant in Phase 1.
